A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same numerical-embedding probing and intervention study. All pages, including Appendices A–C, are readable, and equations, results, and visualizations can be matched across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original probe accuracies, arithmetic error rates, embedding interventions, and representation and attribution analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds regularization analyses and further model-embedding visualizations.

M1.justification: v2 adds L1- and L2-regularized training variants of the sinusoidal probe for the new representation analysis. This is a limited variation in training objectives; the four probe architectures, decoding procedures, and embedding-intervention algorithm remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions study single-token integer embeddings and the same addition, subtraction, and targeted multiplication tasks. Added diagnostics use models already studied in v1; changes in evaluated model sizes do not introduce new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains the same binary, sinusoidal, linear, and log-linear probe comparisons. The original-versus-intervened Llama 3 1B comparison also remains. OLMo 2 32B's removal from arithmetic evaluation changes the evaluated model configuration, not the competing probe methods.

E3.justification: Table 2 changes from measuring the proportion of errors involving undecodable operands to comparing error rates conditional on decodable versus undecodable inputs, substantially redesigning the central error analysis. Prompt selection changes from 1B models to all evaluated models below 20B, and OLMo 2 32B is removed from arithmetic evaluation. The added regularization experiment introduces L1/L2 training treatments.

E4.justification: v2 adds an analysis of how L1/L2 regularization affects learned probe representations and substantially revises the association analysis through conditional error-rate comparisons. PCA visualizations expand from four to seven models and Fourier diagnostics from four to nine. The confidence and head-attribution analyses are retained, with the former moved into Appendix A.2.

E5.justification: Neither version adds seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The 20-fold probing setup and descriptive output-probability boxplots remain; the statement about statistically lower confidence is relocated rather than newly supported by a reported test.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces the earlier error-share results with conditional rates, supporting the new finding of higher errors for undecodable inputs in 8 of 12 configurations. Table 1 also changes values, including OLMo 2 1B addition from 22.21% to 21.39% and Llama 3 3B subtraction from 0.15% to 0.03%, while removing OLMo 2 32B. Changed prompting prevents treating these as same-setting gains. Additional diagnostic results appear, but Figure 1 and intervention reductions remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4), the sinusoidal and binary encodings, and projection definitions are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation appears; the conditional error-rate redesign is an empirical protocol change.

C1.justification: The core claims of accurate numeric decoding and beneficial embedding intervention remain. The conclusion adds a broader claim that these findings undermine the premise and validity of numerical offloading approaches, extending the paper's claimed implications beyond v1.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new conditional error comparisons and proposes different frequency-use explanations for L1- and L2-trained probes. It also explicitly limits the study to single-token embeddings and distinguishes this scope from understanding internal numerical-processing mechanisms.

D1.justification: v2 adds a repository link and announces released implementations, training recipes, and configurations. Appendix B identifies winning prompt numbers by model, and Table 2 specifies exhaustive input combinations. These improve disclosure, although Appendix B's reference to Llama 3 2B conflicts with the evaluated 3B model.

R1.justification: v2 adds Levy and Geva (2025) on digit representations, plus Štefánik et al. (2024) and Spiegel et al. (2025) when discussing future data and architecture improvements. It also strengthens its positioning against the already-cited offloading approaches; the broader related-work framework remains.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. Local revisions rewrite the error analysis, expand the conclusion and experimental details, move model-behavior discussion into Appendix A.2, and add Appendix A.3. Author contribution and affiliation information also changes.

P2.justification: The PCA and Fourier figures gain multiple panels and occupy separate appendix pages, and a new two-panel regularization figure appears. The confidence figure moves from the main text to the appendix. Table 2 gains task-specific decodable/undecodable rows, Table 1 loses a model column, and Table 3 gains prompt numbering.

improvement.justification: The revised Table 2 supplies the missing comparison with decodable inputs, improving evidence for the claimed association. Added diagnostics, prompt details, code-access information, and explicit scope limitations also improve transparency. These gains are limited by the unsupported extension to offloading approaches and removal of OLMo 2 32B arithmetic scores despite retaining claims about its high arithmetic accuracy.
